## NASA JPL and NAIF (ephemerides, constants, rotation)

**Why this family:** JPL Solar System Dynamics and NAIF publish the ephemerides and constants that NASA missions themselves use; positions, rotation models and mass ratios come from here so the app agrees with Horizons.

## Sources considered and not used

Kept here so the reasons are not lost. Details are in the linked notes.

| Source | Why not | Where recorded |
|---|---|---|
| Wikipedia, Wikidata, GeoNames.org, OpenStreetMap, Natural Earth, blogs, aggregators | Not official; the project cites only the publisher of record | [[Rules#Sources]] |
| NGA GEOnet Names Server | Could not be reached from this network (timed out for every try, 2026-11-15); its format and licence were never confirmed. Kept defined but switched off | [[0010-names-databases-for-earth-positions]] |
| UNESCO World Heritage list | Behind a browser challenge (HTTP 403); not fetchable by the pipeline | [[Earth names databases (GNIS, GNS)]] |
| ArcGIS Online copies of official data | A commercial platform; the agency's own service is used instead | [[Earth names databases (GNIS, GNS)]] |
| JPL mean elements for the Moon inside 1800–2050 | JPL warns they are "not intended for ephemeris computation"; measured far off. Used only outside the Horizons table | [[0008-moon-chebyshev-table]] |
| Published limb-darkening coefficients | Could not be verified while planning M2a.1; the Sun's surface is illustrative | [[2026-10-04-m2a1-imagery-and-shading]] |
| NASA PDS Ring-Moon Systems profiles | Need a heavy toolchain; NSSDCA ring fact sheets used instead | [[2026-10-04-m2a1-imagery-and-shading]] |
| Dumoulin 2017, James 2013 (Venus interior papers) | Publisher pages refuse the fetcher and no open copy exists, so the quote cannot be checked | [[Peer-reviewed papers (interior estimates)]] |
| Papers in journals outside the trusted list (MNRAS, Phil Trans, conference abstracts) | Not on the journal list in decision 0009 | [[0009-peer-reviewed-papers-for-estimates]] |
| NASA image-centre coordinates ("Location: 3° S, 37° E") | The centre of a picture, not the place | [[0010-names-databases-for-earth-positions]] |
